claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires configuring PC settings such as enabling Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 or updating BIOS firmware in order to launch.

citations.review_text: i'm extremely disappointed with activision and this game's pc compatibility. i own a lenovo legion t5 with an amd ryzen 7 3700x, tpm 2.0, and secure boot enabled. i've updated my bios from the 2021 version to the 2023 version, updated my tpm firmware to 3.58.0.5, and followed all the recommended troubleshooting steps. even after all that, activision's secure attestation wizard still says my bios firmware needs an update. my pc passes the tpm 2.0 and secure boot checks but still won't pass the bios firmware check. it's frustrating to spend hours trying to play a game i've purchased, only to be blocked by a firmware requirement with no clear solution. activision needs to do a better job supporting pc players and providing solutions for legitimate customers.
Cant even play the game because it says BIOS Update Required but i have everything up to date and settings all set to what they require on their webpage. This game just needs to die off already

-finally build a gaming pc
-install warzone 
-get into game 
-install another 20-30 gigs 
-open the fucking bios to enable secure boot
-wait for shaders 
After all that i can finally play the game
-first match in i get demolished by people that are already prestige master even though the game came out in October
How the fuck does this even happen??why does the matchmaking system think this is a evenly skilled match?
And even after all that bullshit  the gameplay isn't any better, the only guns you will see are the new meta guns

just avoid it at this point, its not worth it

I do not understand how a multimillion dollar game can have such a weak spot, but here we are. I have a specific motherboard with version 3.*.0.*, meaning my BIOS is not compatible with the anti-cheat integrated into this game. Thankfully, I only sunk 3 hours of my life into figuring this out, with the monstrous download time of the game and all. Turns out, if your motherboard is this version, you simply cannot be approved by their anti-cheat, and you cannot play ranked or multiplayer. Didn't even stick around to try campaign because I was so disgusted at the gall of this game I paid SEVENTY-FIVE DOLLARS for and gave THREE HOURS of my life up for, to ask me to update my BIOS firmware???? Are you insane?????? Never mind the fact that with further research, it seems such a firmware update may not even exist for me to implement if I ever found the motivation to do so???? 

TL;DR you shouldn't have to update BIOS firmware to play a video game.

I just wanted to play some Warzone after a long week of working. Downloaded it during the day, so I can play in the evening. After launching it, you realise that it did not download the game. After downloading the game AGAIN, you still can't play. You need to update BIOS because why not. Then you can't play because you don't have TMP 2.0. After 20 minutes of research, you turn it on ON THE BIOS SETUP, because apparently you need to change BIOS settings in 2026 to play with an AAA game. After that, you still can't play because you need to enable secure boot IN THE BIOS AGAIN. Then you can't play because these settings somehow activate Bitlocker, which you did not know that exist and you do not have the 48 digit password for it, so now all your data is lost from the last 6 years because your SSD is locked. And after 1 and a half hour later you sit there with 2 beers, a broken computer, a broken soul and a ruined weekend. I guess some of this is my fault but come on.

I paid good money for a game that won't play until you make some serious changes to your PC settings, with a possibility to brick your PC while doing a BIOS flash. I don't know how COD can be this popular with these requirements. Most people I know would not be comfortable doing that. It should be illigal to sell a game in this state without a big warning before paying. I finally got it running but I can't recommend it at all. 0/10

Needed a BIOS update, Secure Boot, and a TPM reset just to launch this game. Had to convert my drive from MBR to GPT, dig through motherboard revisions to find the right firmware, and flash it myself — genuinely felt like I needed an IT degree to get into a match. A game should not require this level of system surgery just to start. Anti-cheat requirements are one thing, but the onboarding and error messaging around them is a disaster: no clear instructions, no helpful diagnostics, just cryptic “Secure Boot not enabled” and “Failed attestation status” errors that send you down a rabbit hole. Not user-friendly at all.

I shouldn't have to go messing around in my BIOS to play a game. Even after following the Activision instructions, customer support and having secure boot enabled, I still couldn't play because my motherboard manufacturer does not provide the appropriate update to the BIOS that is required to play. You know Activision; Valorant and Battlefield has figured out this anti-cheat thing and it doesn't require me riffling through my BIOS to play them. Refunded.

Secure Boot & TPM 2.0 Not Detected
Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 must be enabled to play some or all parts of this game. Steam has checked your system and one or both of these settings appear to be disabled. You can learn more about this game requirement on the Steam Support Site.

this is some bull shit non of my other game require this crap i will never buy another COD game ever again.

This is extremely bad experenice for such a highly priced game, you will be swimming in tutorials to customize your PC in order to even play the game, i have a few hundred games on steam, and this is by far the hardest to get to work and run, if you wish to actually play the game that you paid for you will not get it here, don't waste your time.

If you do wish to play this game, you will have to modify everything from your bois to your windows build in some cases, and even have use custom software to modify it to make it playable.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience launch failures, crashes, or error messages preventing them from entering the game.

citations.review_text: Gets worse and worse. Can't even launch the campaign! Great job!

piece of dogshit cant even run properly like how is this even in the store when it can't even run? after a few seconds of launching it just stops without any error to show and any solutions etc. like wtf is this?

Don't get too excited about this game and rush to spend your $70. You might want to make sure it actually launches first.

I've spent an entire day trying to get this damn game to run. No error messages, no crash reports, no error codes. Absolutely nothing. Just a game that refuses to launch.

Here's what I've tried so far:

Updated the BIOS.

Enabled Secure Boot.

Verified TPM 2.0.

Installed the latest drivers.

Gone through hundreds of Reddit threads, Steam Community discussions, and AI-generated troubleshooting solutions.

The result? Absolutely nothing.

Apparently, asking a $70 AAA title to simply launch is setting the bar a little too high these days.

Congratulations on releasing a premium-priced game that can't even manage the most basic requirement of being a game: actually running.

What makes this even more disappointing is remembering what this franchise used to represent. Back in 2007, Call of Duty was practically synonymous with quality, innovation, intense action, and memorable storytelling. It was a franchise that set standards rather than struggled to meet them.

Almost two decades later, here we are. The price tag has gone up, but apparently, the quality assurance department didn't get the memo.

From setting the standard for the entire industry to failing at the launch screen. Quite an achievement.

Well done, Activision. Truly impressive.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the multiplayer maps as too large, with poor layouts and problematic spawn points.

citations.review_text: Best Cod since MW 2019, however, the maps are far too big in multiplayer and some of the map design is terrible.

Modern Warfare 4 is my first game within the series I have decided to play for a fair bit. To be transparent, I am more of a Black Ops kind of fellow, but that series has been mutilated by BO6 and 7. Which is why I decided to give MW4 a try. So far, the game is very very well optimized. At the start I had a few hicups with the rendering, but it later fixed its self. The gun play is okay. Like I said, I am a Black Ops guy, and if you remember the older gun play, you can imagine I am probably not a fan of mw4's gun play. It is smooth, but it's not something I like very much. The aesthetic of the game is cool and I like that they're trying to stay consistent with it. The maps though, I am not a fan. They look consistent to the game's aesthetic, which I appreciate, but the layout makes me dread each one. Spawns are funky, the maps are long and wonky, and none of them really standout. The maps make me feel like I am being forced into a particular playstyle. If I have a shotgun, in most maps I need to either camp or use slugshots. It never feels like I can just run around and have fun without dieing on the way to the range I need. And it seems everyone is going with the same meta. I can count on my hands the amount of games someone had a shotgun or sniper. Metas don't completly make me not like maps, but it's the hunch that map developers make the maps to conform to the meta's. More shotguns could be cool. More diverse map layouts and aesthetics would be neat. More insentive to run something other than "meta" would be nice, but the aim of each match is to win, so there isn't much I imagine could be done. Overall, I wouldn't reccomend the game. But it's not bad, that's for sure. However, if nothing else were to be added or improved upon, I would say the game is pretty bad. If you think I am incorrect, let me know, I don't leave many reviews and I am pretty ignorant to the modern warfare series, so I would like to hear some other opinions.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game requires BIOS updates and TPM 2.0 settings to play, which blocks them from launching the game.

citations.review_text: Have to update BIOS and reformat my hard drive to play, which shouldn't ever be a thing especially after downloading a 160+ GB game. Such a let down. Games shouldn't need access to this level of my computer.

"A Security Theater Masterclass That Punishes Everyone Except Actual Cheaters"Rating: ⭐️ / 5 stars

If you want a game that treats its paying customers like suspected cybercriminals while letting actual hackers waltz right through, this is the masterclass. Ricochet’s brilliant anti-cheat logic apparently dictates that the biggest threat to fair gaming isn't the guy wallhacking with a free loader, but a regular gamer whose motherboard BIOS version is off by a single sub-decimal point.

Instead of stopping cheaters—who routinely bypass these kernel-level roadblocks within hours—the hyper-aggressive firmware and TPM requirements function as an elite gatekeeper whose only achievement is locking out normal players. You get to spend eight hours fighting file permission errors, partitioning hard drives, and wrestling with motherboard brick risks just to get a "Failed Attestation" warning for trying to play a casual match.

It’s completely backwards. The cheaters are still flying across maps and aimbotting without a care in the world, while regular players are stuck doing IT troubleshooting on a weekend. Absolute joke of a security system.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the matchmaking system as alternating strictly between heavily one-sided wins and extreme losses.

citations.review_text: The match making in this game is BALLS. I don't think I've had a single game where its like..." wow these guys are my skill level." Nope its that stupid engagement based matchmaking. It gives you one game of spoon fed kills, then the next 2 will be the biggest sweat pits you've ever played in a non ranked game mode that even if you tried you won't win and its not close.

First time giving CoD a shot since MW19 due to the alleged improvements this time around and while the story mode is genuinely impressive, SBMM and aim assist in multiplayer have gotten to the point where matches ONLY rotate between stomping or getting stomped. Even pros are struggling to keep a positive K/D in this game, it's THAT bad. I don't doubt Activision has "the data" to prove that this system works for the majority of zoomers but for several skill brackets, the matchmaking system has officially sucked the fun out of playing almost entirely. 

Add to that the general anti-consumer nonsense (like bundling all of the CoDs together under a single Steam page to hide reviews, which I'm amazed Valve allows tbh) and I wouldn't recommend anyone spend a dime on this or any future Activision titles until their c-suite figures out why people play games again (hint: they're supposed to be FUN, not just monetize-able).

claims.claim: Reviewers complain that PC players cannot disable crossplay, forcing them to play against console players using aim assist.

citations.review_text:
PC players can't disable cross play but console players can.

I'm tired of these aimbot controller monkeys b-hopping like baboons in every gunfight.

Aim assist is broken and we don't even get the option to avoid these trogs.

❌ NOT RECOMMENDED. CROSSPLAY IS RUINING THE MULTIPLAYER EXPERIENCE

I bought the latest Call of Duty expecting to enjoy the multiplayer, but instead, I’m extremely disappointed.

Playing against console players with aim assist is an incredibly frustrating experience. Gunfights often feel unfair, and instead of enjoying the game, I constantly find myself fighting against what feels like an excessive aiming advantage. It seriously ruins the experience for PC players.

Why should PC players have to suffer because of forced crossplay? Why can’t we have a proper option to disable crossplay and play exclusively against other PC players?

I paid my hard-earned money for this game to have fun, not to deal with frustrating and unbalanced multiplayer matches. The current system makes it feel like fair competition takes a back seat to keeping cross-platform matchmaking enabled at all costs.

DEVELOPERS, PLEASE ADDRESS THIS ISSUE!

Here’s what needs to change:

* Add a proper option for PC players to completely disable crossplay.
* Rebalance console aim assist to ensure fair and competitive gunfights across all platforms.
* Give players the freedom to choose which platforms they want to play against instead of forcing cross-platform matchmaking on everyone.

Until these issues are addressed, I cannot recommend this game. What’s the point of buying the latest Call of Duty if the multiplayer experience is more frustrating than fun?

NOT RECOMMENDED. Please stop ignoring the concerns of your player base and start taking multiplayer balance seriously. Players deserve a fair competitive environment, not a system that makes them question whether buying the game was even worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign is exceptionally good and stands out as one of the best in recent years.

citations.review_text:
MP was great in the pre-season, could have fun with guns and builds, players were not overly sweaty but everyone was still out to win it. Now in season 1 it feels like the fun has successfully been optimized out of the meta. Meta builds are here, the sweats have migrated, and playing for fun puts you at a serious disadvantage. 

Single Player was fantastic and for me was worth the price and felt like they actually hired writers this time around, but if that's why you want to buy this I recommend sailing the seas and finding it elsewhere, or wait for a good sale.

DMZ was great for a bit, with people running missions and tense standoffs for objectives with opportunistic squads much like ARC, but with much less friendly interactions(which i enjoyed not having to negotiate situations). Now its all fully kitted extract campers with kits too expensive to do anything but sit on the final exfil thanks to perks that show its location. Don't waste your time unless extraction shooters are your thing and if that's the case -- why are you even here when EFT exists?

I've enjoyed my time logged in the pre-season with the game, but doubt I'll be back much unless its to replay campaign. It could've been MW2019 2.0.

MW4 Campaign Review

10/10 Voice Acting
9/10 Mission Design
9/10 Serious Tone Story Telling 
9/10 Memorable Characters
8/10 Replay Value
10/10 Graphics
8/10 Optimization 

Overall Campaign Rating: 9/10 Best COD Campaign in forever!

Multiplayer and DMZ Requires up to date Bios Firmware which sucks major ass and it super annoying

Campaign is PEAK and it was the only reason I purchased this game. Did played Multiplayer for a while like maybe about 8-7 matches but not interested in that. The Campaign missions are awesome. Interesting new characters specially Ko-Jin-Hyuk. Overall, worth it if you are going for the campaign.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that DMZ mode suffers from players camping extraction points for easy kills.

citations.review_text:
MP was great in the pre-season, could have fun with guns and builds, players were not overly sweaty but everyone was still out to win it. I've enjoyed my time logged in the pre-season with the game, but doubt I'll be back much unless its to replay campaign. It could've been MW2019 2.0.

I was absolutely loving the new DMZ (which I specifically got the game for)...

...and then I got killed by a rat, camping an exfil... just I was about to jump in the chopper...
Sigh... that really sucks. No idea how people are lame enough to camp exfils for easy kills, but Infinity Ward have given the lamest players an easy strat to make them feel good about themselves... that really sucks, but fine...

And then... 

50K+ to buy my guy back!?!? or I lose my hard earned progress?!?!

What the actual fuck?!!?

I had no idea that was a thing! The thought never even occurred to me! It's just such a mindboggling dumb thing that I just exited the game in dismay and disbelief. Losing all your gear and loot for the run is an understandable punishment, but the buyback bullshit?! And the price keeps getting even more expensive?!

I was so looking forward to playing a ton more DMZ, but now that I know that there is a MASSIVE punishment for being killed... it just completely killed my desire the play the game. Especially when there will always be lame ass extract campers...

Please Infinity Ward, get rid of the buyback cost! It shouldn't be a thing!

Or better yet, give us a PvE only mode! There many games that have implemented PvE modes that prove players REALLY want it. There are many, many players that are not sweats... I dare say most. We just want a relatively chill shooting experience to come home to after a long tiring day at work, and we want to be able to do it in a large awesome map with all types of missions, bosses, vehicles, etc... 

and no... there are no other game comparable to this DMZ map, missions, bosses, unlocks, etc... 

Until they remove this unbearably oppressive punshment mechanic it is a hard pass for me. I've gone way past the refund window, so I guess I'll have to play the multiplayer mode instead, which sucks, because I only got the game for the DMZ mode.

Man, I am so bummed now...

**After 40 Hours in DMZ ONLY:**

*Pros*:

- Great sound design and audio quality. (for the most part)

- Enjoyable gameplay and gunplay.

- Pretty beginner-friendly compared to other extraction shooters.

- Easy to jump into without an overwhelming learning curve.

*Cons*:

- A lot of Warzone players still treat DMZ like a Battle Royale rather than an extraction shooter.

- Possem perk is still an issue, even after the recent adjustments.

- PvP often overshadows looting, missions, and actually extracting.

- Risk vs. reward is completely unbalanced. You can spend an entire raid looting multiple compounds and still walk away without finding a single blueprint worth extracting with.

- Loot needs to feel more rewarding, especially considering the time and risk involved in each deployment.

- User Interface is to clutterd, way to much forced UI during in game action, no ability to minimize/hide DMZ Orders or Kill bar.

best cod campaign of all time multiplayer is only good because of shipment

I hate Call of Duty. And I say that with some regret, because I used to be a huge fan of the franchise. I've played pretty much every COD since the early days, and after years of disappointment, I honestly didn't expect much anymore. Then I played 10 hours of this campaign, and without exaggerating, these are probably the best 10 hours I've spent on a COD in easily a decade.

First, the game is very well optimized. It's absolutely nothing like the beta. Infinity Ward's new in-house engine does a great job. The lighting, effects, design and textures all look fantastic. For once, Call of Duty actually feels up to date technically. Took them long enough.

The campaign itself is just great. The music is insane, the story is great, and the whole thing feels like old-school COD again. I don't want to make a 1000-word review about it, so I'll just say this: if you were a big fan of the golden age of Call of Duty, you'll probably love this.

Last year we lost a great man in the video game industry, Vince Zampella. This campaign genuinely feels like a love letter to him. Thank you, IW, for not forgetting where you came from.

I'll update this review once DMZ and multiplayer are out. How the game is supported and updated over time will also play a big part in my final opinion.

I only play MW4 Multiplayer (mouse and keyboard) so this review will strictly only cover MW4 MP. No campaign, no Warzone, no DMZ.

First of all, this game desperately needs input-based matchmaking or just any way to opt out of playing against controller players. The amount of auto-aim assistance they give controllers is criminal. Any semblance of aim skill has been taken out of a game that's all about aiming and shooting at people. Either nerf aim assist by like 50% or let me opt-out of those clownfest lobbies.

Secondly, SBMM/EBMM/EOMM is so egregious in MW4 to the point where I am playing against the exact same 20-30 players every single day I get on the game (in EU). This is like 3 weeks post-launch with cross-play forced on (to my great dismay) at peak hours and all this game has to offer me are 1-2 active lobbies that are available to me that contain the exact same people I've been playing with and against ever since I first bought the game. 

I'll sometimes exit out of a match, re-queue and it will put me in the exact same lobby 3-4 times in a row until I give in and let it re-join me in the same lobby again. Its completely ridiculous.

Third, the multiplayer maps are awful and are clearly designed with camping in mind. They have no flow, the layouts are terrible if you like running and gunning (which is what CoD has always been about) and reward hardcore camping and moving as little as possible compared to older CoD games. Perks like Ninja and Ghost are a must-have due to the super loud footsteps and the map layouts that consistently reward angle-holding and camping.

Fourth, base game + Season 1's content has been very lackluster. Not nearly enough variety in weapons and many iconic guns are just completely absent. The 3 new guns that are included in Season 1 are cool and all but they're far from enough considering the life cycle of a CoD game nowadays. Same goes for the base maps as well as the new maps in Season 1. We've payed 70€+ (or 100€+ if you're a VE…

# Aim Assist Is Out of Control, Maps Feel Unbalanced — PC Players Need Better Options

I really want to enjoy Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but the current state of controller aim assist, map design, and overall multiplayer balance is making the experience frustrating and, honestly, not very enjoyable.

**Controller Aim Assist Needs to Be Balanced**

I understand that controller players need some aim assist to compete against mouse and keyboard players. However, it feels like the aim assist in this game has gone way too far. I've had situations where I hit an enemy four to fifteen times, only for them to instantly turn around, jump around, spin nearly 180 to 360 degrees, and spray me down before I can even react.

PC players have traditionally had the advantage of precise aiming with a mouse. That advantage doesn't seem to mean much anymore when controller aim assist appears to track targets so aggressively, especially when players are constantly jumping, sliding, and spinning during gunfights.

The difference in my matches has been noticeable. I used to regularly finish games with around 40 kills and 10 deaths. Now, I'm often struggling to get 5–10 kills while dying repeatedly. I understand that not every bad match is the game's fault, but too many gunfights feel unfair and inconsistent.

There needs to be a separate PC-only matchmaking option or a serious adjustment to controller aim assist. Players who prefer mouse and keyboard should have the option to compete against others using the same input method. Crossplay can remain an option, but controller aim assist needs to be balanced so that it helps players aim without feeling like it does too much of the work for them.

**The Maps Feel Too Small and Unbalanced**

Another major problem is the map design. Too many maps feel extremely small, chaotic, and unbalanced. I would really like to see more medium-sized maps that offer a better balance between close-range combat, mid-range gunfights, and opp…

- Flinch, bob, and sway force your aim off target (controller players have less of a problem with this since AA still tracks when you are getting hit)
- You can't use movement to beat AA, jumpshotting has been nerfed so it throws you off target- again, AA tracks for a controller player while they jump.
- Aim assist reacts instantly- it is like giving someone perfect reaction times- 0ms. As a kbm player, you are stuck with human reaction times and imperfections.

We are playing two different games. It is completely unfair for one group of players and Activision is too scared to admit the truth. Spend your money on Battlefield 6 for a game that is actually fair and doesn't have punishing matchmaking.

If you play with a mouse, you’ve been lied to—regarding PC optimization, aim assist, and the balance between mouse and controller players. It was supposed to be a 50/50 split, but it’s more like 90/10 in favor of aim assist; they lied without even batting an eye. They claimed to be aiming for "realism"—visual recoil, flinch when taking damage, and so on—which sounds fine, but on a mouse, you actually feel it. Meanwhile, controller players have zero recoil thanks to an absurdly overpowered aim assist. They claimed to have reduced it more than ever before in the game's history, but they also slowed down character movement—effectively canceling out any changes. In the end, aim assist is actually stronger than it has ever been; it’s so sticky that you could play with your feet and still get kills. It’s basically a legal aimbot—who knows what else they’ve cooked up? Don’t even get me started on the audio; it was supposed to be "realistic," but it’s the usual garbage—you can tell if an enemy is to your left or right, but forget about figuring out if they’re above or below you. PC optimization literally doesn't exist; they lied in their promotional material about everything that might have attracted PC players. The only thing that actually works is the expanded FOV—everything else is absolute, 99% pure shit. Don’t buy this if you play with a mouse. Buy it if you’re a brainless Yeti—or want to become one—or if you cheat in games; this is essentially a legal aimbot. citations.review_text:
This is not a review of any particular Call of Duty title. It’s strictly a vote against forcing all players to be funnelled through this dreadful universal app for the latest Call of Duty titles. I originally purchased this as “Modern Warfare II” and had to live through the horror of that purchase being cannibalized into this awful centralized “Call of Duty” hub that did nothing but make launching the game I bought a cumbersome nightmare that more often than not just feels like an endless cycle of updating and relaunching the game multiple times to actually play the game I want to play. The first thing I did when Modern Warfare II was  liberated from this app last year was uninstall it from my PC, and the only reason I have it again is for Modern Warfare 4.

To the developers: please consider giving users the option of launching Modern Warfare 4 on its own without forcing us to go through the hub for the next 2-3 years. Also, please do some housekeeping and maintenance on your older titles such as fixing bugs and actively banning cheaters who ruin the older titles as they are sunsetted. There are still many players who actively play the older titles and it’s unfortunate when developers become negligent in keeping them functioning correctly. Modern Warfare II currently has a bug that prevents users from opening and modifying the settings for the campaign. In the meantime, I look forward to the day Modern Warfare 4 is freed from this awful application so I can once again remove it from my PC.

The worst update in Warzone history – completely unplayable right now.

Honestly, this latest Warzone update is a complete disaster. It feels like a massive step backward for the franchise, and it’s getting to the point where I don't even want to log in anymore.

First off, the movement is total trash. It feels heavy, clunky, and unresponsive compared to what we're used to. On top of that, the graphics look super mediocre at best—there is zero next-gen feel to it, and optimization seems completely ignored.

What makes it even worse is how they treat their player base. People drop real money on skins, weapon blueprints, and cosmetics, only to find out they can't even use the weapons they built or paid for. Locking custom weapon progress/loadouts after an update and forcing everyone to play with whatever garbage preset guns they hand out at the start is completely absurd. What's the point of grinding or spending money on loadouts if the game locks you out of them?

This is hands down the absolute worst update this game has ever received. The current season is tragic, frustrating, and a complete waste of time. I wouldn't recommend playing this current season to anyone. Save your time and money until (or if) they fix this mess.

To make matters even more ridiculous, even items unlocked through the previous Battle Pass are affected. I literally unlocked a knife from last season's Battle Pass—it shows up in my inventory, but the game has it locked and won't let me equip it. You can't even level up the guns you're using, and custom crafts you spent time building are completely unusable. It makes zero sense.

Rating: 1/10
